idea: Embodied carbon assessment and reporting for real estate funds
buyer: Real estate fund managers with disclosure obligations
pain: Embodied carbon reporting is mandatory-adjacent and nobody in-house understands construction
verdict: Two-domain fit with a regulatory driver; crowded by sustainability consultancies but she brings the finance lens.

why.distribution: Warm fund contacts, and real estate teams are a findable segment within them.
why.demand: Disclosure pressure is real and budgets exist, though sustainability consultants already hold the work.
why.fmf: Architecture gives genuine construction literacy; carbon accounting itself is a discipline she would be learning.
why.revenue_structure: Annual reporting cycles bring repeat work without a contract.
why.defensibility: Methodology plus accumulated building data; large consultancies compete hard.
why.time_to_revenue: A first portfolio in 1-3 months through a warm contact.
why.tailwind: Disclosure obligations tightening across UK and EU with real budget attached.
why.ceiling: £16k x 13 portfolios = £208k, close to full delivery capacity.

ceiling_arithmetic: £16k x 13 portfolios = £208k gross less ~£10k data = £198k. Thirteen portfolio assessments is near full-time. Realistic part-time: 5-6 = £80-96k.
carries: Regulatory driver, two-domain credibility, and fees high enough that few clients are needed.
kills: She would be entering an established consultancy market with a credential she is still building.
test: Ask three real estate funds who does their embodied carbon work and whether they are satisfied.
test_pass: They describe a gap between the carbon consultants and the investment team.
test_fail: Their sustainability consultant handles it end to end.
